qti-item-body.p: A researcher asks a random sample of 114 Dutch 16- to 18-year-olds how many glasses of alcohol they drink in a typical week. The mean is 6.11 glasses, the standard deviation 4.29 and the standard error of the mean 0.40. The data are strongly skewed to the right.

img.alt: A histogram of the number of glasses of alcohol per week for 114 young people. Most of them drink between 2 and 8 glasses; the bars then get lower and lower to the right, with a long tail up to about 22 glasses. The distribution is clearly skewed to the right.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Thanks to the central limit theorem, which conclusions are correct? Select all that apply.
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The sampling distribution of the mean is approximately normal.
The sampling distribution of the mean is skewed to the right, just like the sample.
A 95% confidence interval for the population mean runs from about 5.3 to 6.9 glasses a week.
About 95% of young people drink between −2.5 and 14.7 glasses a week (6.11 ± 2 × 4.29).
With a sample this large, the drinking habits in the population must be approximately normally distributed.
